headline: Avoiding Common Mistakes in Smoke Damage Cleanup
articleBody: When you're dealing with smoke damage, it's easy to make a few missteps that can actually worsen the problem or prolong the odor. Let's talk about some common mistakes to avoid. First, a big one is trying to clean everything yourself without the right protective gear. Smoke residue can be toxic, so always wear gloves, masks, and eye protection. Another mistake is using the wrong cleaning products. Regular household cleaners might just spread soot or set stains, making them harder to remove. You need specific products designed to break down smoke compounds. Don't forget about porous materials! Trying to wash smoky drapes or upholstery in a regular washing machine might not remove the embedded odor and could even damage delicate fabrics. It's often best to leave these to professionals. Also, a common oversight is not addressing the HVAC system; smoke particles get into the ductwork, and simply running your AC will just circulate the smell. Finally, avoiding professional help too long can let odors set in deeper, making the job much tougher.
